$description: The COPY for REVIEW-icons-2026-09-16-v1.html (#277 lane RI). Every {placeholder} is filled at build time from dry-run.json and from live counts over knowledge/. No integer is typed into this file or into the HTML.
title: Icons and logos into the graph — #277 lane RI
headline: {n_nodes} new nodes, {n_edges} new edges, and four questions.

decisions.title: Do the icons enter as icons AND groups, as the icons alone, or not yet?
decisions.lede: The manifest holds {n_icons} glyphs under {n_groups} group keys, and there are {n_logos} logo lockups. All three kinds together are **{n_nodes} nodes**. The group hubs are not decoration: without them, **{n_isolated} icons carry no edge at all** — they have no active twin, no ruling, and no component renders them — and the family arrives as a fog of dots. With `inGroup`, every one of the {n_icons} has at least one edge and the family has ten legible hubs.
decisions.why: Take (a). The ten hubs cost {n_groups} nodes and {n_ingroup} edges and they are the difference between a navigable family and {n_isolated} unreachable dots. The payload is measured, not estimated: {payload_kb} KB against the explorer's {explorer_kb} KB, **+{payload_pct}%** on bytes and **+{node_pct}%** on node count. That last number is a look, not an argument — judge it on the screenshots below, and if it is too much, (d) costs nothing.
decisions.attrib: Lane RI wrote this recommendation, re-deriving every figure from icons.manifest.json and the live tree. Lane IX (#277, ca294b4) costed the same three options first and reached the same place.
options: Icons only — {n_icons} icon: nodes, no group hubs. {n_isolated} of them arrive with no edge at all.
Groups only — the {n_groups} hubs, and nothing hanging off them.
Not yet. Nothing enters; the proposal stays on the shelf.

decisions.title: Draw component → icon from the geometry byte-match?
decisions.lede: There are two routes and they are not close. The **byte-match** compares every inline <path d> in every reference snippet against the {lib_keys} distinct normalised path keys in the library, using _validate_icons.py's own norm() — the gate that already polices icon sources. It finds **{n_usesicon} pairs across {n_usescomp} components and {n_usesicons} icons**, and resolves every one to a manifest slug. The **prose** route — the slug as a word in the meta — fires on **{prose_hit} of {prose_metas} metas** and makes **{prose_pairs} pairs**, because accessibility, no, time, user, card and block are all icon slugs.
decisions.why: Take (a). The number that settles it is not {n_usesicon} against {prose_pairs}; it is **{struct_only}**: that many components render a library glyph and never once say the word “icon” in their meta. The prose route would have missed every one of them while inventing {prose_pairs} pairs of English. Four limits travel with the edge and are written into the schema text: it measures the reference snippet and not the contract (so it is usesIcon, never requiresIcon); {n_usesicons} of {n_icons} icons are used, so it lights up a twelfth of the family; {unmatched} inline paths match nothing and get no edge; and sprite <use> refs mean the pair set is right but per-use frequency is not measured, so no weight goes on the edge.
decisions.attrib: Lane RI wrote this recommendation and re-derived the byte-match independently from the gate's own norm()/DRE. Lane IX found the route and the {struct_only} figure first; s274-D12 and s276-D5 are the refusals the prose route runs into.
options: Draw it as usesIcon — {n_usesicon} edges, from the byte-match, with the four limits attached.
Wait. The icons enter as nodes; no component→icon edge is drawn in this wave.

decisions.title: Fifteen bases have two or three “active” glyphs. Is the bare one the default?
decisions.lede: active is a boolean on all {n_icons} records and it is exactly predicted by the slug — {n_active} records end -active or -active-N, with zero mismatches either way. {n_multi} bases carry more than one: dentist has three, fourteen others have two. activeVariantOf draws all {n_avo} twins whichever way this goes, so nothing is blocked. What is open is whether one of them is the active twin.
decisions.why: Take (a), and know that it is a small ruling rather than a measurement. The evidence for it is one file: _validate_icons.py's twin arm already computes the expected twin as slug + "-active" — the gate has been assuming the bare form is the default since it was promoted. And it works here: **all {n_multi} of the multi-variant bases have a bare -active**, so (a) resolves every one of them and leaves exactly {n_extra} extras declared. If that assumption is wrong anywhere, (b) costs nothing — the {n_avo} twins are drawn either way and only defaultActive waits.
decisions.attrib: Lane RI wrote this recommendation. The gate's assumption is read from knowledge/_validate_icons.py's active_names(); lane IX flagged the ambiguity as blocker B4 and left it yours, which it still is.
options: The bare -active is the default, by rule. The {n_extra} -active-2/-active-3 records enter as declared variants.
Leave it open. Draw the {n_avo} twins, draw no defaultActive, and the {n_multi} stay a declared null.

decisions.title: Ten of the twelve logos are bound by nothing. Do they enter anyway?
decisions.lede: s230-D2 names two — masterbrand-light-colour and masterbrand-dark-colour — and those are your words. The other {n_unbound} are bound by nothing measurable: _rules-index.json holds {logo_rules} rules whose file is logos.md, {logo_rulings} rulings name a logo .svg in governs, and logos.md itself says the standard lives on create.hsbc and there are no design tokens. Four masterbrand-identifier and four hexagon files are referenced by nothing in the corpus at all; the two mono files are used by template-auth and only by template-auth.
decisions.why: Take (a). Twelve nodes cost about {logo_kb} KB and the unbound ten are the point, not the cost — eight lockups that nothing references is exactly the condition s230-D2 was written to fix, and a graph that shows them greyed and rule-less puts that in front of you instead of leaving it in a folder. Every one of the {n_unbound} enters carrying a declared governedBy null that says what is missing and whose it is.
decisions.attrib: Lane RI wrote this recommendation. The {logo_rules}-rules and {logo_rulings}-rulings figures are re-measured here; lane IX named the same gap as blocker B3 and put it off-repo, where it stays.
options: All {n_logos} enter — the {n_unbound} unbound ones visibly so, each with a declared null naming what binds it (nothing).
Only the four masterbrand files that actually ship in a snippet.
Logos wait for a rule source that does not exist yet.
